title: Range Rover L322
verdict: A Munich-engineered, Solihull-built limousine that still walks up a rock garden on its tiptoes. Buy the paperwork, not the paint. The timing chains decide whether it's a bargain or a boat anchor.

paragraphs: The third Range Rover was a clean break. The [[range-rover/p38|P38]] had wrapped new electronics around old Land Rover hardware. The L322 threw out the ladder frame and the beam axles and started again: a unitary body, independent air suspension at all four corners and, at launch, BMW engines and electronics. Purists called it heresy. Then they drove it off-road and found that its cross-linked air springs let the wheels droop and stuff much like the old live axles did. Twenty years later it's the cheapest way into a properly capable luxury 4x4, and a minefield for anyone who buys one without receipts.

story.heading: THE BMW RANGE ROVER FORD LAUNCHED
paragraphs: Under BMW ownership the project was codenamed L30. Joint Rover and BMW teams developed it, first at BMW's FIZ research centre in Munich and then at Solihull for the final stages. The plan was to share electronics and core engines with the E38 7 Series. Then BMW sold Land Rover to Ford about two years before production started, though the contract kept BMW involved until volume production was under way. Ford renamed the project L322, and the truck went on sale in 2002, arriving in North America as a 2003 model.

That handover explains the L322's three engine eras. Early petrol trucks used BMW's 4.4-litre M62 V8 (286 PS), and outside North America there was a BMW 2.9-litre Td6 diesel. For the 2006 model year Ford switched to Jaguar's AJ-V8 in 4.4-litre (305 PS) and 4.2-litre supercharged (400 PS) forms, behind a six-speed ZF. The 2010 facelift brought Jaguar Land Rover's 5.0-litre V8s: 375 PS naturally aspirated, 510 PS supercharged.

story.heading: A LIVE AXLE IN DISGUISE
paragraphs: The off-road trick was in the plumbing. MacPherson struts at the front and double wishbones at the rear ride on air springs, and the valves linking each side's springs can make the suspension behave like a live axle when the truck is crossed up. Permanent four-wheel drive runs through a chain-driven two-speed transfer case that can shift between high and low on the move. Early trucks used a Torsen centre differential with a 50:50 split that could send up to 65% of torque to either axle.

From the 2007 model year the L322 got the Terrain Response system from the LR3 and Range Rover Sport, a lockable centre differential and, on Supercharged models (optional elsewhere), an electronically locking rear diff. That year also brought stiffer anti-roll bars and air springs, and the TDV8 twin-turbo diesel replaced the BMW six outside North America. Later updates revised the sand, rock-crawl and hill-descent programs, added hill-start assist, and the 2011 4.4 TDV8 with ZF's eight-speed automatic.

story.heading: LIVING WITH ONE NOW
paragraphs: The L322's reputation is mostly about three failures. The BMW M62's nylon timing-chain guides go brittle with age and break, and a broken guide can wreck the engine. The 5.0-litre V8 has its own chain-tensioner and guide wear, and replacing the chains is a big, specialist job. The air suspension, as on every Range Rover since, eventually needs compressors, springs and height sensors. Owners who keep L322s running long-term replace the guides before they fail, service the 'sealed for life' gearboxes anyway, and treat a diagnostic tool as standard equipment.

Get past that and the truck rewards you. Running parts are cheap from aftermarket suppliers, Atlantic British publishes free how-to videos for most routine jobs, and the aftermarket offers sump guards, bush kits and sensor-rod lifts. A well-sorted 2007–2009 or a documented 2011–2012 is one of the most comfortable ways to reach a trailhead. With a sensor-rod lift and all-terrain tyres, it will keep going after the trailhead too.

story.heading: LEGACY
paragraphs: Land Rover built 293,494 L322s before the all-aluminium [[range-rover/l405|L405]] replaced it in 2012. It set the template every Range Rover since has followed: monocoque body, four-corner air suspension, and electronics deciding how the power reaches the ground. Atlantic British's ROVERLOG blog says it ranks second only to the [[range-rover/classic|Classic]] in Range Rover fans' affections. In its day it was the truck that bridged the gap between a [[land-cruiser/100-series|Land Cruiser 100]] or [[lexus/lx470|LX 470]] and a [[g-class/w463|W463 G-Class]] — plusher than the Toyotas, more road-friendly than the Mercedes.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · SPECIAL EDITIONS
callout.title: Anniversaries, Autobiographies and an armoured Vogue
paragraphs: Late L322s were sold with plenty of special editions. North America got a 20th Anniversary edition of 40 supercharged trucks in pearl white. The UK had 30 Claret-painted supercharged 35th Anniversary cars. The 40th Anniversary Autobiography Black ran to 700 cars, and the run-out Autobiography Ultimate Edition (500 cars) came with rear-seat iPads, a refrigerator and reclining climate-controlled rear seats.

The oddest one was built for people with enemies. In 2007 Land Rover offered an Armoured Range Rover Vogue, developed with Armour Holdings and certified to the European B6 ballistic standard. In 2010 Overfinch built a Holland & Holland edition, with the gunmaker acting as design consultant.

engineering_intro: The L322 swapped Land Rover's traditional ladder frame for a stiff steel monocoque and replaced live axles with four-corner independent air suspension. Off-road ability comes from software and plumbing instead: cross-linked air springs that imitate axle articulation, a two-speed chain-drive transfer case, a centre diff that was a Torsen until 2006 and lockable from 2007, and traction control on every corner. Engines came from three owners: BMW (2002–05), Jaguar (2006–09) and JLR's own 5.0 V8s (2010–12).

engineering.note: The first unitary-body Range Rover, with a 2,880 mm (113.4 in) wheelbase.
Struts at the front, wishbones at the rear. Cross-linked valves imitate live-axle articulation off-road.
High and low range can be selected on the move. A Torsen T-2 centre diff (50:50, up to 65% either way) until 2006.
Terrain Response arrived for 2007. An electronic rear locker was standard on Supercharged and optional on other models.
286 PS (BMW), 305/400 PS (Jaguar), and 375/510 PS for the 5.0 NA and supercharged.
The GM five-speed was paired only with the Td6 diesel. The eight-speed came for 2011 with the 4.4 TDV8.

generations_table.note: ZF 5-speed auto. Plastic timing-chain guides are the known weak spot.
GM 5L40-E auto. Never EPA-listed (not sold in the US).
Jaguar engines, ZF 6-speed. Terrain Response and a locking centre diff from MY2007.
LED lights, TFT instrument panel. Check the timing-chain tensioner and guide history.

buying_checks.head: Demand timing-chain paperwork
buying_checks.body: On 2003–2005 BMW-engined trucks, look for receipts for chains and guides, or budget for them. The nylon guides go brittle and break, and owners report failures clustering around 130,000–170,000 miles. On 2010–2012 5.0s, check for tensioner and guide updates. Listen for a rattle on a cold start.

buying_checks.head: Cycle the air suspension through every height
buying_checks.body: The compressor should be barely audible. Grinding means it's on its way out. Watch for slow rises, a lean, or warnings. On 2003–05 trucks, corroded or seized height sensors can stop the truck adjusting without leaving any fault codes.

buying_checks.head: Test low range and the range-change motor
buying_checks.body: Select low and back again with the truck stationary. A range-change motor that has seized from lack of use can cost about £1,000 to fix. Make sure Hill Descent Control works too.

buying_checks.head: Treat 'sealed for life' gearboxes as unsealed
buying_checks.body: Hesitant shifts or warning lights point to gearbox trouble. Ask whether the fluid and filter have ever been changed. Atlantic British recommends a service every 60,000 miles on later ZF six-speeds, including the leak-prone valve-body sleeve. A rebuild costs about £2,000 in the UK.

buying_checks.head: Listen at full lock
buying_checks.body: Knocking at low speed on full lock can mean a front differential problem, and many were recalled. Clonks over bumps from the rear point to perished hub bushes.

buying_checks.head: Read the codes before and after the drive
buying_checks.body: A pre-purchase diagnostic scan is cheap insurance. Read the codes before and after a long test drive, because sellers can clear faults just before you arrive. Check that every warning light comes on with the ignition and then goes out.

buying_checks.head: Hunt for water and oil
buying_checks.body: Check for water in the rear fuse box and under the carpets. Check the M62 for valve-cover and other oil leaks, and look for white coolant streaks around the expansion tank. Expansion tanks fail.

buying_checks.head: Check the brakes and wheels
buying_checks.body: L322s are hard on brakes; expect discs and pads about every 30,000 miles. Avoid 22-inch wheels with low-profile tyres, which ride badly and pinch-puncture easily.

repairs.title: Ride height sensor replacement (2003–2005)
repairs.symptoms: The air suspension won't change height or adjusts erratically, often with no stored fault codes. The sensor pivots seize, and cracked rear sensor bodies let water in, which corrupts the readings.
repairs.fix: Rear: the sensor sits against the rear subframe on the lower control arm. Clean and unplug the connector. Undo the 13 mm-head bolt and nut that hold the link to the arm, then remove the two screws holding the sensor to its bracket (they're often rusted, so use penetrating oil and locking pliers). Fit the new rubber-bushed sensor with its new screws, check that the arm moves freely, refit the nut while holding it with a 10 mm spanner, and pack the connector with dielectric grease. The front sensors are done the same way.
repairs.tools: 10 & 13 mm spanners · penetrating oil · locking pliers · dielectric grease · LR020627 (FR) / LR020626 (FL) / LR032106 (rear, both sides)

parts.name: Rear ride height sensor set x2 (RQH100030, L322 2002–2009)

repairs.title: BMW M62 timing chain guides (2003–2005 4.4)
repairs.cost: About £600 in parts (owner figure). Atlantic British's complete kit TCKL322 lists at $1,849.95
repairs.symptoms: Clatter on a cold start, more chain noise as the engine ages, or in the worst case an oil-pressure light. Nylon guide debris can block the oil pickup.
repairs.fix: With the engine in the car, remove the front of the engine, the valve covers and the sump. Replace the upper and lower chains, the centre and outer guide rails, the tensioners and the tensioner arm, and fit new timing-cover, valve-cover and VANOS seals. Owners say getting the crankshaft nut off is the hardest part (one used a homemade locking bar and a scaffold-pole extension). Drop the sump to check for guide fragments while you're in there.
repairs.tools: M62 engine timing/setting tools · crank-locking bar · breaker bar · 32 mm deep socket (ground down) for solenoids · VANOS seal tool · kit TCKL322 or equivalent

parts.name: Valve cover gasket set RH + LH (BMW 4.4, 2003–05)

repairs.title: Cold-start rattle: VANOS seals and non-return valves
repairs.cost: Valves cost a few pounds each. A VANOS seal kit and tool run about £120
repairs.symptoms: A brief rattle on a cold start that goes away on a quick restart, on a BMW 4.4 whose guides may still be fine.
repairs.fix: Before condemning the chains, change to a good fully synthetic 5W-30 or 5W-40 with a quality (Mann or genuine) filter. Owners report the rattle stopping after the filter change alone. Next, replace the VANOS solenoid seals and the oil non-return valves behind the solenoids. Some say the real culprits are two non-return valves in the block under the head gasket. If it still rattles, move on to the tensioners and then the guides, which means dropping the sump.
repairs.tools: VANOS seal tool · ground-down 32 mm deep socket · quality oil filter

parts.name: Genuine oil filter LPW500030 with housing gasket (BMW 4.4, 2003–05)

repairs.title: Transfer case range-change faults
repairs.cost: About £1,000 if the motor has to be replaced
repairs.symptoms: A chime and a warning message, then the transfer case drops into neutral. Low range engages but high won't, or a 'trans failsafe' message appears.
repairs.fix: Rarely used range-change motors seize, and their contacts wear. Check that the connections under the transfer case are clean and plugged in. Try the reset owners use: fit a spare 5A fuse in position 37 of the main fuse box, cycle the ignition, remove the fuse, then cycle the hi/lo selector. One owner fixed worn contacts by taking off the contact cover under the case and adjusting them. Replace the motor if it has seized.
repairs.tools: 5A fuse · contact cleaner · basic sockets · diagnostic tool

repairs.title: Differential and transfer case oil change (2003–2005)
repairs.cost: About $220 for a kit with oil and new drain/fill plugs
repairs.symptoms: An overdue service. Old oil breaks down and collects condensation, and water in the diffs or transfer case destroys bearings.
repairs.fix: Drain and refill the front differential, rear differential and transfer case from their drain and fill plugs, using new plugs. Atlantic British recommends doing this every 60,000 miles.
repairs.tools: Drain pan · fluid pump · socket/hex set · Atlantic British kit DTCM200A

parts.name: Castrol SAF-XO 75W-90 differential fluid TYK500010 (front / non-locking rear)
Castrol BOT 26 transfer fluid STC4861 for the NV225 box (search)

repairs.title: ZF six-speed transmission service (2006–2012)
repairs.time: ≈ 1 hour (owner estimate; one dealer quoted 7 hours)
repairs.symptoms: Slow or harsh shifts, fluid weeping from the valve-body connector sleeve, or a high-mileage 'sealed for life' gearbox that has never been serviced.
repairs.fix: Drop the pan with its integral filter, replace the leak-prone valve-body sleeve, fit a new pan and gasket, and refill with ZF Lifeguard fluid to the correct level. Atlantic British recommends doing it every 60,000 miles. Some owners also fit new valve-body 'bridge' seals as preventive maintenance.
repairs.tools: Atlantic British kit TRANSM300SKA (pan, sleeve, 7 qt ZF Lifeguard) · fluid pump · torque wrench · scan tool for fluid temperature

parts.name: ZF 6HP26 service kit: pan/filter LR007474 + sleeve TZV500010 + 7 qt fluid
DA2142 steel pan + separate filter conversion kit (ZF 6-speed)

repairs.title: 5.0 V8 timing chains (2010–2012)
repairs.cost: Genuine kit TCK5030 lists at $1,499.95. The special tool kit lists at $1,249.95
repairs.symptoms: A rattle on cold starts from worn tensioner-to-guide contact. Ignore it and the chain can jump timing or snap.
repairs.fix: Atlantic British says this job is not recommended for DIY. It means stripping the front of the engine, replacing all three chains, the guides, shoes and tensioners, and usually the water pump, thermostat and cam sprockets as well. Fit the updated parts and keep the receipts, because buyers will ask for them.
repairs.tools: TCK5030 kit · TCK5030TOOL timing/crank tool set · crank holding tool · front seal tool

parts.name: 5LTCK genuine 5.0 V8 timing chain kit, 34 pieces
Primary drive belt 5.0 (LR064185) — replace while the front is apart

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: On 18-inch wheels, owners say 265/60R18 (about 30.5 in) fits with no problems, including off-road. 265/65R18 has been warned against because it can rub when the air suspension drops. On 20s, 275/55R20 clears the bump stops but rubs the liners at full steering lock. Check that a taller spare still fits in the well.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: Thirsty. The EPA rated a 2004 BMW 4.4 at 11 mpg city, 15 highway and 12 combined; a 2008 4.4 or 4.2 Supercharged at 12/18/14; a 2011 5.0 at 12/19/15; and a 2011 5.0 Supercharged at 12/18/14. The tank holds 100 litres.
3,500 kg (7,716 lb) braked and 750 kg unbraked. A 2002 4.4 HSE weighs about 2,430 kg at the curb.

faq.q: Which years and engines should I buy or avoid?
faq.a: Owners and buyers' guides generally rate the 2007–2009 Jaguar-engined trucks best: Terrain Response, a locking centre diff and the six-speed ZF. Buy a 2003–2005 BMW 4.4 only with receipts for timing guides (or if you'll do them yourself). Buy a 2010–2012 5.0 only with evidence that the chain tensioners and guides have been updated.

faq.q: Does it have low range and lockers?
faq.a: Every L322 has full-time four-wheel drive with a two-speed chain-drive transfer case you can shift on the move. 2003–2006 trucks use a Torsen centre diff and open axles with traction control. From 2007 the centre diff can lock under Terrain Response, and an electronic rear locker was standard on Supercharged models and optional on others.

faq.q: How do I lift an L322?
faq.a: The usual way is longer ride-height sensor links. Atlantic British's RHSRAL322 rods make the air suspension think it's low, so it holds about 2.5 in of extra height all the time, enough for bigger all-terrains. Its listed fitment is 2005–2012 trucks.

faq.q: Is the air suspension a deal-breaker?
faq.a: No, but budget for it. Springs leak, compressors fail slowly and noisily, and 2003–05 height sensors seize. Genuine parts are expensive (a full air-ride restoration kit for 2003–05 trucks lists at about $2,450), but each part can be replaced on its own. Some long-term owners convert to coils after spring failures.

faq.q: Are the gearboxes really 'sealed for life'?
faq.a: No. Early petrol trucks use a ZF 5HP24, and Td6 diesels use a GM 5L40-E that Australian testers call so bad owners treat it as a service item. Both left the factory with 'sealed for life' stickers. Atlantic British recommends a fluid and filter service every 60,000 miles on the later ZF six-speed.

faq.q: How do I tell which engine I'm looking at?
faq.a: For US trucks, go by model year: 2003–2005 is the BMW 4.4, 2006–2009 the Jaguar 4.4 or 4.2 supercharged, and 2010–2012 the 5.0 or 5.0 supercharged. Parts suppliers split their catalogues the same way, so order by engine as well as year.

faq.q: My BMW 4.4 rattles on cold starts — are the guides gone?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Owners trace many short cold-start rattles to VANOS seals, solenoid non-return valves or a poor oil filter. One owner's rattle stopped after switching to a Mann filter. A rattle that keeps getting worse, or that shows up with low oil pressure, is a different matter. Stop driving and check the guides.

Yes. Club 4X4 calls it great off-road, and its cross-linked air springs are designed to mimic live-axle articulation. On any truck you're considering, check that low range engages and that Hill Descent Control works. The usual first mods for trail use are a sump guard, a sensor-rod lift and all-terrain tyres.

mods.why: Longer height-sensor links trick the EAS into running about 2.5 in higher, with no new springs or software needed.
A 6 mm alloy sump guard protects the sump, front diff, bumper and radiator, and bolts to the front subframe.
Rebuild the EAS once, properly, before a trip: compressor, rear springs and front strut assemblies.
New front arms and polyurethane bushes cure wander and clonks on high-mileage trucks.

who.name: Atlantic British control arm kit CA-L322

mods.why: The L322 wears through brakes fast. Full disc-and-pad kits make the 30,000-mile refresh simpler.
Timing-chain and PCV kits for the BMW 4.4 deal with its two best-known weak spots before they strand you.

baseline_service.intro: Assume nothing was done. The L322 spans five petrol and diesel engines and three transfer boxes, so confirm exactly what you have (engine, model year, open or locking rear diff, NV225 or DD295 transfer box) before ordering a single fluid. Land Rover's differentials and DD295 transfer box take an exact measured fill, not 'fill until it drips', and the friction-modified fluids are not interchangeable.

items.spec: BMW 4.4 (2002–05): fully synthetic to ACEA A3/B3, ≈8.5 L refill · Jaguar 4.4/4.2 SC (2006–09): 5W-30, ≈7.7 L with filter · 5.0 NA/SC (2010–12): 5W-20 to WSS-M2C925-A, 8.0 L · 3.6 TDV8: 5W-30 to WSS-M2C913-B/-D (STJLR.03.5003), ≈9.5 L service fill · 4.4 TDV8 (2011–12, DPF): 5W-30 to WSS-M2C934-B / STJLR.03.5005, 9.0 L

items.note: The DPF diesels must have low-SAPS oil to the exact spec. Owners warn against overfilling the Jaguar V8: put in 6–6.5 L, run it, then top up to the dipstick.

On the 6-speed the filter is built into the plastic pan, so a new filter means a new pan; replace the leak-prone valve-body sleeve while it's off. Fill and level at temperature per the workshop procedure. Drain-and-fill, don't pressure-flush.

items.spec: Front: Castrol SAF-XO 75W-90, 0.75 L refill · Rear non-locking: SAF-XO, 1.14 L · Rear electronic locker: Castrol SAF Carbon Mod Plus 75W-90 (LR019727), 1.55 L
items.interval: Then every 60,000 mi (Atlantic British recommendation). Land Rover's 2006–08 US schedule: electronic rear diff at 75,000 and 150,000 mi; front and rear axle oil every 10 years
items.note: Identify the rear diff first: the electronic locker has a cylindrical motor on top with a cable. Pump in the exact quantity rather than filling to drips, which overfills and aerates the oil. Diff plugs often seize, so crack the fill plug before you drain anything.

parts.name: Castrol SAF-XO 75W-90 TYK500010, 1 L (front / non-locking rear)
Genuine rear electronic locking diff fluid LR019727 (1 qt)

items.spec: Texaco Cold Climate PSF 14315 · reservoir ≈1.6 L
items.interval: Check level and hoses at purchase. Land Rover's 2006–08 US schedule only checks and tops up the fluid, with no replacement interval
items.note: Look for weeping at the rack and pump hoses while the truck is up on stands.

items.spec: Shell DOT4 ESL, or a low-viscosity DOT4 meeting ISO 4925 class 6 (2011 handbook)
items.interval: Change at purchase if undated; then every 3 years regardless of distance (Land Rover owner guides, LRNA 2006–08 schedule)
items.note: The low-viscosity spec matters for the ABS and stability system. Standard DOT4 is for topping up only.

items.spec: BMW 4.4: primary LR051050 + A/C belt · 5.0: primary LR064185 + secondary belt
items.interval: Replace at purchase if the age is unknown. LRNA's 2006–08 schedule replaces the drive belts at 150,000 mi and the supercharger belt at 105,000 mi
items.note: Addicted Motors' 'must-do' L322 kit puts both belts on the list alongside the transmission service and front control arms.

items.spec: Compressor, drier, valve blocks, air springs and height sensors
items.interval: At purchase, then whenever the truck sits low after standing
items.note: Leave it overnight and measure each corner. Time how long the compressor runs. On 2003–05 trucks, height-sensor faults often store no code. Replace the compressor relay with the compressor: it's a known weak point.

items.interval: At purchase on diesels [CONFIRM IN MANUAL for the diesel interval]; Land Rover's 2006–08 US petrol schedule replaces it at 150,000 mi
items.note: On the 2006–09 Jaguar petrols the filter is part of the in-tank sender assembly, so it isn't a routine item.

items.spec: Load-test the battery; check charging voltage
items.note: Low voltage on an L322 throws a cascade of unrelated air-suspension and transmission warnings. Rule out the battery before you chase faults.
